newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain union, employer leaders approve labour reform.
newsitem.headline: Spain union, employer leaders approve labour reform.

text.p: Spain's employers and unions said on Wednesday their respective executive bodies had now approved a labour reform deal and it would be signed next Monday.
Unions and employers finished drafting a deal at the beginning of April after months of intense talks. The accord was expected to win overwhelming approval by the two sides executive bodies.

The General Workers' Union (UGT) said the deal was almost unanimously approved by its regional leaders on Tuesday. The Workers' Commissions union (CCOO) said 80 percent of its leaders voted in favour of the accord.
The employers' association CEOE said its board of directors had approved the deal on April 15.
After the signing, the government will then examine ways of converting the proposals into legislation.
The government hopes reforms will go part of the way toward liberalising Spain's highly rigid labour market and suppressing its steep unemployment -- the highest in Europe at just under 22 percent.
